transcript:
alex: Hey, hitting a weird one on prod-gpu pool — several inference pods serving streaming gRPC responses are pausing mid-stream for ~2-5s then resume. GPUs sit at 0/100 utilization during the pause. Anyone seen gRPC chunking stalls like this?

priya: Ugh, seen similar on a different cluster. Usually network fragmentation or offload weirdness. Any tcpdump/iperf data?

alex: I pulled logs from the serving pods — gRPC stack shows repeated retries, stream window not advancing. kube-proxy logs show nothing. Linking excerpt:

```
2026-02-10T09:21:03Z grpc: stream send blocked for 2304ms
2026-02-10T09:21:05Z grpc: connection reset by peer
2026-02-10T09:21:05Z grpc: stream resumed
```

alex: Also noticed node kernel logs with GSO warnings when high concurrent streams hit a node: "rx: skb unaligned, dropping offload" (paraphrasing).

josh: Can you repro with iperf between two GPU nodes? Need to see if it's general east-west or just pod overlay.

alex: Ran quick checks:
- iperf3 (tcp) between host IPs: 9.8 Gbps steady
- iperf3 (udp) with 1500 MTU: moderate packet loss spikes
- ping with large payload: `ping -M do -s 1472 <pod-ip>` -> fragmentation / no reply intermittently

maya: That ping result screams MTU blackhole / PMTU issue. What CNI? VXLAN or IPIP? and host MTU vs overlay MTU?

alex: Using calico IP-in-IP overlay with host NIC MTU=9000 (Jumbo), calico configured overlay_mtu=1450 (we inherited this). Some nodes had /etc/cni/net.d/calico.conf showing mtu=1440; others 1450. There's a 10-byte mismatch across nodes.

priya: Mixed MTU across nodes + large host MTU + GSO/TCP offloads = fragmented segments landing with wrong metadata. gRPC streams use many small writes but sometimes batch into large frames at kernel offload level -> when an intermediate path can't handle the oversized segment you get stalls.

josh: Checked `ethtool -k` on affected nodes? Are GSO/GRO/TSO enabled inconsistently?

alex: Yep, found variation. Sample:
```
ethtool -k eth0
  tcp-segmentation-offload: on
  generic-segmentation-offload: on
  tcp-udp-fragmentation-offload: off
```
On some hosts TSO was off (older kernels/provisioning image) and others on.

maya: So we have 3 orthogonal mismatches: CNI mtu values (1440 vs 1450), host NIC jumbo MTU=9000, and offload flags inconsistent. All combine to create occasional fragmented packets not handled by overlay -> gRPC stalls.

priya: Root causes sound clear. Quick mitigation options:
1) Enforce a consistent calico/overlay mtu across cluster (e.g., 1400) and roll configs.
2) Disable GSO/TSO on host NICs as a short-term mitigation (`ethtool -K eth0 tso off gso off gro off`).
3) Enable PMTU probing: `sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1` to avoid blackholes.
4) Add a per-node kube-proxy/iptables rule to MSS clamp on SYN: `--clamp-mss-to-pmtu` on the iptables POSTROUTING for overlay.

josh: MSS clamping + consistent CNI mtu looks safest short-term. We should avoid disabling offloads long-term due to perf hit on GPU serving.

alex: Agreed. Proposed immediate plan:
- Patch calico DaemonSet config to uniform mtu=1400 (rollback window 30m). Test on staging first.
- Add a kube DaemonSet that runs `ethtool -K` commands for any node still mis-provisioned (ad-hoc) for emergency.
- Enable tcp_mtu_probing=1 cluster-wide via a sysctl DaemonSet.

priya: One nit: changing calico mtu will require flannel-style reconfig? With calico it reassigns routes, but pods may need restart to pick up new iface MTU. We'll do rolling node drain on canary subset.

maya: For verifying, create a small harness that streams a large gRPC response repeatedly (simulate model token streaming) and measure stalls before/after. I can script that.

alex: I'll open a short incident ticket and run staged rollout.

infra-bot: Incident ticket created: INF-2026-1187. Priority: P2. Links: https://redwood.atlassian.example/browse/INF-2026-1187

josh: One more test to validate: capture `tcpdump -i vxlan.calico -s 0 -w /tmp/vxlan.pcap` during a repro and look for fragmented packets lacking DF flag or mismatched lengths. Also run `ss -tin` on the node during a stall to see retrans patterns.

alex: Will collect pcaps and ss output. Early observation: stalls correlate with bursts of ~64KB writes from the runtime (gRPC batching) that seem to get split incorrectly.

priya: After canary, if mtu change fixes it, follow-up: add provisioning check to our node bake pipeline that enforces calico.conf mtu and ethtool offload defaults. Also add e2e test that streams 1MB gRPC payloads across the cluster to catch regressions.

maya: I pushed a quick gRPC harness to `gitlab.com/rw-infra/grpc-repro` — test script `run_stream_test.sh` will exercise 50 concurrent streams for 5m. Use it in staging with and without the mtu change.

alex: Timeline: will run staging canary in 30m, if green start rolling 10-node batches across prod GPU pool. I'll post results here.

priya: Thanks — and if we still see issues after mtu harmonization, will look at kernel bug w.r.t GSO metadata in our kernel versions. Might need a microcode/kernel bump on old nodes.

josh: Keep me tagged. If we need to emergency-disable offloads I can push a daemonset-run immediately.

alex: Update: staging canary passed 15m of continuous streaming with no stalls after calico mtu->1400 + MSS clamp. Moving to prod canary now.
